svg.text: The whole of FOXHUNT 2 / ROMAN 1 on one page. Nothing collapsed, nothing on a second tab.
893 × 1263 CSS — density 0.7. 135% of the A4 card's line count.
17 STEPS · TOT 07:40L · HOLD THE RING TO TICK A STEP
T/O 75% fuel. Rejoin WP1 at FL100, lead checks speed.
Tank SHELL 06:57–07:09. Hold WP3 in TRAIL. Push 07:22L.
FENCE at WP4 — EMCON, RWR silent, off-set card .5x1.5, NOE.
Pop-up gate WP6, level by WP7. IP CENTURION, TOT 07:40L.
Laze WP8 @FAO3, confirm shack, egress WP14 NOE south.
The shipped greys exist so a recon photo does not blow out against its surround. A dense
text card is the opposite problem — it wants maximum contrast at small sizes, which is
exactly what paper has and what a 4.2:1 mid-tone ceiling cannot give. Warm paper,
near-black ink, dark section bands. Threat red and the go green were both re-picked to
hold up on a light ground rather than a mid one.
A 44px lane on the right, one ring per row. A tap does nothing; the ring fills clockwise
while the press is held and only commits at the end — shown mid-fill on HOLD. Under
turbulence or with a pen on a tablet, a single stray tap must never mark a step flown,
and a wrongly ticked step is worse than an unticked one because it reads as progress.
The A4 card pilots already fly sits at 14 arcminutes — 10pt Helvetica at arm's length.
My earlier floor of 20′ was a reading-a-document threshold, not a glance-at-a-card one.
The Crystal Light resolves down to about 11′. So there was far more density available
than the first mockup used, and it was designed at 93% of paper for no reason.
No PLAN / CARD split. Paging to find your bullseye mid-flight is exactly the failure a
kneeboard exists to prevent. Threats, callsign, bullseye and loadout live in a 76px
header band above the route; comms, tankers and the game plan sit below it. Only the map
is a second page, because it is an image.
It needed 642px and the old surface was 625. At 893 it needs 561 and leaves 316px of
slack — so STEP, REF, ALT/SPD and NOTES all read on every row, the way the LaTeX does.
Nothing is hidden behind a selection any more.
The first mockup quietly stopped at RTB. This carries the recovery too: feet wet,
marshal, push, Case I approach, trap, and the bolter-to-divert line. That is the part
you actually need when it is going wrong.
CURRENT STEP IS EMPHASIS, NOT EXPANSION
HOLD is raised with a go bar and reads NOW; flown steps carry a tick and dim. Nothing
collapses, because there is no longer a reason to hide a row to make space.
Laser code alone was never enough. Each target now carries waypoint, lat/long,
description, weapon and code on one line.
The status text was right-aligned over the CARD / MAP keys — a 30px overlap. Status,
page keys and window controls now each have their own lane, measured rather than
WHAT IT COSTS IN THE HEADSET
At a 40° quad this sits at 14′ — exactly paper parity. At 45° it is 15.7′, better than
paper. At 35° it drops to 12.2′, still above the 11′ floor but tight. Quad size is the
real control, and it belongs to OpenKneeboard until we own the layer.
